coverage.category: 1. Household employers: domestic workers, live-in carers, nannies
coverage.found: INSS 1979 domestic-service regulation: employer must register the worker and report hires/exits within 3 working days. Compliance very low (La Prensa 2016: under 10% registered; 26,591 insured vs 200-280k estimated workers). No dedicated product found. Households will not pay and the duty is rarely enforced. Weak, see candidate C07.

coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers
coverage.found: No current Nicaraguan register, police permit or purchase-book rule found. Only historic export bans (1961/1963) and a 2014 La Prensa note: collection centres may not buy from municipal collector crews, used batteries are restricted, fines C$5,000-50,000. Nothing new.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: Pawnshops (casas de empeño) are UAF sujetos obligados: a 2016 press note says they report monthly, including sales of unredeemed pledges once the monthly total reaches USD 3,000 (threshold not confirmed in the primary text). CONAMI register is K03. UAF duty is a different duty, see C02. General second-hand dealers: no rule found.

coverage.category: 4. Gold and jewellery buyers
coverage.found: Jewellers and precious-metal/stone traders are UAF sujetos obligados under Ley 977 and the UAF activities-and-professions normativa: monthly sales reports (local sales from USD 5,000, exports from USD 10,000), client profile, 5-year records, annual external audit and manual. No MEM/MIFIC gold-buyer register found; the Ley 387 concession covers commercialisation. 2026 press says new gold exporters shipped about USD 100M to the US in 2023-26 (La Prensa fetch returned 403, unread). See C01 and C11.

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: No dismantler register found. Used and new vehicle dealers are UAF sujetos obligados (cash sales of USD 5,000+ used and USD 10,000+ new, monthly report), see C01. A parts or scrap dismantler regime was not searched separately.

coverage.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K04. IPSA CUBE farm-code traceability is government-run and free. Livestock transport permits were not confirmed for Nicaragua; the results that mentioned a transport guide were from Costa Rica.

coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: IPSA Resolución 063-2024 (La Gaceta 171, 13 Sep 2024) sets sanitary and physical requirements and meat inspection for authorised bovine and pork establishments. Municipal rastros need a municipal permit under the environmental norm for slaughterhouses. UNA thesis shows weak compliance in municipal rastros. Few private buyers, municipal customers. See C10.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: Only IPSA Resolución 032-2021 (EU honey export requirements, La Gaceta 59, 25 Mar 2021). No beekeeper or apiary register or recurring report found. Nothing buildable.

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: IPSA licenses vet establishments and regentes under Ley 291/862 and NTON 20001-15; regente licence renewal is done online on the IPSA SINAIP portal (sinaip.ipsa.gob.ni). A free state portal exists, so the gap is small. See C04.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: ANA Nicaragua resolution RATN-ANA-001-2021 (under Ley 1046 reforming Ley 620) creates a register of consultants and well drillers. The FAOLEX PDF is image-only, so requirements, fees and renewals are unread. Small group. See C08.

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: No specific register for septic or sludge haulers found. General MARENA permit regime under Decreto 20-2017 and norm NTON 05 014-02 for non-hazardous waste; municipal licences likely. Unverified for this activity.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: The search returned only Spanish and Argentine regimes. No Nicaraguan regulation for periodic lift or boiler inspection was confirmed. MITRAB/Ley 618 is the likely frame but is not verified.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: CAPS (water committees) are regulated by Ley 722 and its regulation (consolidated text La Gaceta 217, 29 Nov 2023): municipal registration certificate, then central registry. The authority is named as INAA in older text and ANA in a later version (conflict). No periodic report format found. See C07.

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: Ley 274 and Decreto 49-98: single pesticide register, regente required for larger establishments, MINSA Dirección de Farmacia sanitary licence (registration fee C$5,000 in the document seen), and an annual report by the authority. No recurring dealer-level report found. See C05.

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: Código del Trabajo art. 16 and Acuerdo Ministerial JCHG-004-04-07 (La Gaceta 109, 11 Jun 2007): private employment agencies register with MITRAB, may not charge workers. Renewal and reporting details not found. See C06.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: Ley 198 (1976) on private cemeteries (application to the Junta Local de Asistencia Social) and Decreto 394 (1988) sanitary rules. About 60 funeral companies in 2020 (Confidencial via Observador). No current recurring filing found. Weak, see C13.

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies: associations, charities, halal and kosher supervision
coverage.found: Ley 1115 (2023) puts OSFL oversight under the Ministerio de Gobernación / MINT; a 2025 Normativa Prudencial adds registration, reporting, financial disclosure and sanctions. Cancellations for missed financial statements are frequent (more than 5,600 closed since 2018; 12 more in April 2026 by Acuerdo 06-2026-OSFL). Politically sensitive and risky as a product. See C09. Halal/kosher: not applicable.

coverage.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
coverage.found: Ley 524 and Decreto 42-2005: concession or licence from MTI (intermunicipal) or municipalities, cooperatives need an operating licence, tariffs reviewed every six months. No 2025-26 rule change found. Moto-taxi is rejected in K08. Nothing new.

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: Casas de cambio are UAF sujetos obligados with monthly reports (press note, thresholds unverified). Money changers are in K08 (rejected, politically sensitive). Market traders and street vendors: no register found. Nothing new beyond K08.

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
coverage.found: Food: MINSA licencia sanitaria through SILAIS plus registro sanitario (5-year validity) with RTCA GMP; sources 2011-2023, so artisanal treatment is unconfirmed. Driving schools and nurseries: no Nicaraguan sources found (results were from other countries). Tattoo studios and hunting outfitters: not searched, hunting not applicable. See C14.

coverage.category: 21. Fuel stations and fuel or LPG distributors
coverage.found: Licensing under Ley 277 and Decreto 39-2011 (MEM Dirección General de Hidrocarburos, INE enforces). LPG retailers must show licence, official INE price sign, 20-lb extinguisher, LPG-handling training certificate; wholesalers give INE inventory data and report accidents within 24h. No periodic (monthly) report found for small retailers. Sources are 2006-2012 so currency unverified. No candidate scored 3+.

coverage.category: 22. Grain, coffee, cocoa and other commodity traders, millers and warehouses
coverage.found: Coffee: Ley 2013 caficultura creates RUCN (producers, internal traders, beneficiadores, exporters); exports via CETREX/VUCEN; MAG reports 94 exporters in 2025. No registry found for grain collectors or silos (Ley 930 covers producers only). Coffee export docs are already covered by VUCEN (K06) and EUDR (K02, K07). One weak candidate.

coverage.category: 23. Co-operatives, credit unions and savings groups
coverage.found: Ley 499 reformed by Ley 1233 (Gaceta 9, 17 Jan 2025); INFOCOOP is regulator, director now appointed by the Procurador. Pre-reform duties: sealed minute and accounting books, financial statements to authority within 30 days of year end (art. 108), management report (art. 49). UAF also registers cooperatives as obligated subjects (a UAF 2025 resolution cancelling a cooperative's registration exists; page returned 503 on fetch). Post-2025 duties not confirmed.

coverage.category: 24. Private clinics, labs and other health providers that bill insurers or state schemes
coverage.found: Only background: INSS buys services from EMP/CMP by per-capita capitation (PAHO), supervised by MINSA. No 2024-26 rule, licensing register or claims-reporting duty found. Per-capita payment means little per-claim billing, so weak fit. Not scored.

coverage.category: 25. Pharmacies, medicine importers, and users of controlled chemicals or precursors
coverage.found: Ley 292 (consolidated text in Gaceta 2, 9 Jan 2024), MINSA is regulator; regente farmaceutico files all procedures; psychotropic/narcotic control book must be rubricated and sealed by MINSA (fee C$50, 2002 reform); Ley 177/285 controlled substances need MINSA authorisation; customs and MINSA reconcile controlled-substance imports quarterly. MINSA Resolucion Administrativa 0020-2025 puts medical-device import procedures online. Rubricated paper book limits software value.

coverage.category: 26. Security, cleaning and manpower agencies, and the firms that hire their workers
coverage.found: Private security: Ley 903 (2015; consolidated Gaceta 9, 18 Jan 2024), licence de operacion from the Policia Nacional; regulation and filing duties not found. Cleaning and manpower agencies: nothing found. One unverified candidate.

coverage.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors and suppliers: site registers, accreditation, local-content reports
coverage.found: Mining: 299 concessions (MEM, 2023); Ley 1128 reform led to cancellation of 20 inactive concessions in Dec 2023; gold export needs VUCEN exporter registration plus UAF registration (32 gold exporters listed). Concessionaires must allow artisanal mining under Ley 387. No construction-contractor register or local-content report found. Sector is politically sensitive (US Treasury sanctions on Direccion General de Minas, 2022).

coverage.category: 28. Notaries, land agents, real estate brokers and other professionals with periodic or anti-money-laundering reports
coverage.found: Ley 1129 (Gaceta 8 Sep 2022): real estate brokers need a MIFIC licence valid 5 years, must register each agent, register with UAF within 30 business days, keep records 10 years, include beneficial-owner certificate for company parties; fines up to US$350. Notaries and lawyers are obligated subjects (Ley 977 via Ley 1000; Ley 1113 of 2022) and register with UAF through the Poder Judicial; CPAs through the Colegio de Contadores. UAF Resolution UAF-N-023-2023 governs registration. 10-day reply to UAF requests.

coverage.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals: guest registers, tourism levies
coverage.found: Ley General de Turismo 1210 (Gaceta 141, 2 Aug 2024) and INTUR Reglamento Tecnico for tourism service providers (INTUR-2024-151, Gaceta 236, 20 Dec 2024). Neither text was reached, so guest-register, short-term-rental and levy duties are unverified. No short-term-rental registry found.

coverage.category: 30. Small exporters and importers facing traceability or certification rules: food, fish, timber, forest-risk commodities
coverage.found: Timber: Decreto 45-93 forestry regulation requires industries to keep INAFOR-sealed intake/output books; transport permits from forestry guides (INAFOR Res. 44-2014). Exports run through VUCEN (K06). Cattle is killed by the state system (K04). Fish and food exporters: no search, not reached.

coverage.category: 31. NPO (OSFL) annual financial filing, Ley 1115 (country-specific)
coverage.found: All registered NPOs must file CPA-certified financial statements in paper with the Ministry of the Interior DGRC-OSFL by 28 Feb each year, plus a project report, donor agreements and a DGI tax-return copy, and upload data to the MINT portal within 3-5 days. Audit required at C$50M or more. Fines C$5,000-10,000, up to revocation. Regulation is Decreto 01-2023. Many NPOs have been cancelled for non-reporting. Political risk is high.

coverage.category: 32. Beneficial-owner registry and corporate powers (Ley 1035, Ley 1282 of 2026) (country-specific)
coverage.found: Companies must update the beneficial-owner declaration at the Registro Publico every 12 months and on any change. Initial deadlines ran Apr 2021 to Apr 2022. Ley 1282 (Gaceta 111, 19 Jun 2026) requires representation powers to be registered in the Registro Publico Mercantil or the acts are ineffective, and sets record-retention rules (5 years for firms, 10 for NPOs). No deadline or penalty found for Ley 1282.

coverage.category: 33. UAF monthly reporting by non-financial obligated subjects (vehicle dealers, pawnbrokers, casinos, remittance agents) (country-specific)
coverage.found: A 2019 decree (Gaceta 25 Apr 2019, via press) lists monthly UAF reports: remittances of US$500 or more, transfers of US$5,000 or more, pawnshop sales of unclaimed items at US$3,000 a month, casino prizes of US$1,000 or more, real estate sales of US$100,000 or more, vehicle sales of US$10,000 (new) and US$5,000 (used). Source is old press, so currency is unverified. Registration rule is UAF-N-023-2023.

coverage.category: 34. Coffee single register RUCN, mills and internal traders (country-specific)
coverage.found: RUCN requires beneficiadores, internal traders and exporters to register. Relevant to the existing K02/K06/K07 ideas. No new duty found.

coverage.category: 35. Mining concessions and gold export registry (country-specific)
coverage.found: Gold exporters register with VUCEN and UAF (32 listed). Ley 1128 allows cancellation of inactive concessions. Very small buyer pool and sanctions context; related to rejected K08.

result.reason: The UAF does regulate casas de empeño y préstamo and casas de cambio under Ley 793. It publishes a ROS guide for pawnshops, and its normativa requires compliance officers and AML plans. The press note says monthly reporting applies. I could not read the primary text, so the USD 3,000 threshold, the monthly cadence, penalties and the current in-force status are unconfirmed. A 2023 Bloomberg Línea piece says the UAF was still debating how to regulate pawnshops and cambistas, which conflicts with the other sources. No commercial software was found, but the UAF probably supplies its own reporting formats. The sector is small, with no count found. Nicaragua's political risk is high, since the state controls the regulator and money changers are sensitive, as in K08. Payment is likely low and a sale would be a niche compliance-officer tool. Sources: leybook doc 18388, UAF ROS guide, laprensani 2018, Bloomberg Línea 2023.

Duty is partly real: Ley 1210 (Gaceta 141, 2 Aug 2024) requires providers to register in INTUR's Registro Nacional de Turismo and renew licences yearly (EY summary). Decreto 15-2024 and INTUR-2024-151 exist. I could not read the law text (INTUR PDF returned 503), so penalties and the lodging-specific guest-register duty are unconfirmed. An older INTUR regulation, undated in the results, describes a sealed paper guest book, a monthly report, and a 2% INTUR room charge declared by day 10-15. No lodging software or INTUR portal found, but only 2 searches were run. Market size not found. Filings are paper-based or go through INTUR and the rules are opaque, so willingness to pay is low and the market is small.
